title: Sweep Before You Change
hook: Fog hides the right. Sweep before you move.
scene: Fog sits on the right glass in a work zone at midday. Cones pinch the right lane shut. You need left. The Ledger has blind spots a Beetle never had — a whole van-length of nothing the seat cannot see, and a side mirror that shrinks what is in it if you only look once. The thermos is still empty. Your eyes want the opening, not the sweep.
decision: You need the left lane. What do you look at, and in what order?

options.text: Glance the left glass once and go — you already know the right is cones
options.result: You take the left on one look. A motorcycle you never owned is in the blind spot the side mirror would have shown. He stands on it. You stand on it. The cones get a new story.

options.text: Watch the opening until it is yours, then check the glass as you commit
options.result: The opening closes while your eyes are in it. You drift. A cone kisses the side of the bus. The sweep you skipped was the only thing that would have told you the gap was already gone.

options.text: Left glass, right glass, side mirror, over the shoulder, then the gap
options.result: You run the sweep. The side mirror has a motorcycle in it that the inside mirror missed. You wait one more gap. When you take it, he is already past you.

options.text: Trust the side mirror alone — it sees more than the inside mirror
options.result: The side mirror shrinks a pickup into a toy. You take the gap on a toy. He is a wall. You put the Ledger's shoulder in his.

debrief: The Ledger has blind spots you cannot see unless you sweep them. Glass, side mirror, shoulder, then the gap. Deac runs that sweep every time the Ledger changes lanes.

source.psdp_skill: Skill nine: multi-lane roads – part one
source.teaching_target: Mirror sweep plus over-the-shoulder before a lane change; the side mirror lies if it is the only look.
